summary: Tree-lookout replacement on Dutch Joe Ridge near Winslow, built around 1939-40; sources disagree on design; listed as gone.

facts.design: Timber tower with 7x7 wood-frame cab, 99 ft (1940 plan CT-1); 1939 reports say steel 110 ft and wood 100 ft

events.note: June: steel tower 110 ft to replace the tree lookout; September: 100 ft wooden tower being built by a CCC camp
1940 plan entry, not confirmed as built: CT-1 timber tower, 99 ft, 7x7 wood-frame cab, on private property adjoining the National Forest; tower replaces an earlier tree lookout
Virdia Haught, rancher, in charge; had been working for the Forest Service for several seasons
Blaze endangered the area in June; station, two lumber camps and a ranch reported intact at noon Friday; lumber camps evacuated

evidence.quote: Dutch Joe Ridge is about 60 miles south of Winslow.

evidence.supports: was to replace an earlier tree lookout (1939 plan; 1940 entry says it replaces one)
evidence.quote: The tower replaces an earlier tree lookout.

evidence.supports: June 1939 steel tower, 110 ft, to replace the tree lookout
evidence.quote: A steel fire lookout tower, 110 feet high, is to replace the Dutch Joe lookout tree
Fred Merkle, supervisor, said the tower will be 100 feet high and constructed of wood.
The CCC camp at Chevelon canyon is building the tower.

evidence.supports: two-room caretaker cabin at the base
evidence.quote: A two-room cabin will be built at the base for a caretaker.

evidence.supports: 1940 CT-1 timber tower, 99 ft, 7x7 cab, on private property adjoining the forest
evidence.quote: A plan CT-1 timber tower 99-feet high with a 7x7 wood frame cab constructed on private property that adjoins the National Forest.

evidence.supports: 1944 rancher in charge at the lookout
evidence.quote: Virdia Haught, rancher, is in charge at Dutch Joe lookout, on the Chevelon district south of Winslow.

evidence.supports: employed by the Forest Service several seasons
evidence.quote: He has been employed by the Forest service during the past several seasons.

evidence.supports: June 1956 blaze; station and ranch still intact at noon Friday
evidence.quote: The Dutch Joe lookout station, two lumber camps, and a ranch which earlier had been reported endangered by the blaze were still intact Friday at noon
The lumber camps had been evacuated to avoid possible entrapment of personnel.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on design: June 1939 steel 110 ft, September 1939 wood 100 ft, 1940 CT-1 timber 99 ft (the 1940 entry reads like a plan, not confirmed as built). The White Mountain CCC article (wmicentral.com) returned HTTP 429 and was not read; its search snippet names a Teco R-6 timber design, Geeson Bros. fabricator and a 1940 CCC build. Check it before adding. Record ownership 'federal' conflicts with the 1940 entry 'private property that adjoins the National Forest'; a human should check, no correction proposed. No source describes the site today; access left unknown in facts. A 1948 Forest Service photo (#454121) is captioned on the westlookouts Arizona index, but no image URL was found, so no photo is added. A NARA public-domain image appeared in search (site returned 403) and is not used.
